Authored, not derived. ⚠️ I BUILT THE DERIVATION FIRST AND IT WAS ROUGHLY HALF WRONG on name-matched rows: Waystone read as 'underplace' from 'ways' when it is a BRIDGE-BUILDERS' TOWN; the FORward Archive read as a fort from 'ward'; the Harborward read as a fort when it is a HARBOUR; Millbrook read as 'works' from 'mill' when it is a farming village. ⛔ SAME FAILURE AS THE WATER-WORD REGEX. _distinctFromTier: ⚠️ `tier` is SIZE, `role` is FUNCTION, `kind` is SHAPE — what it looks like from outside. A waygate and a village are both `tier: settlement`; they should never share an icon.

_vocabulary.gate: a threshold in a wall or a border, walked not stepped through
_vocabulary.town: a working settlement, roofs and a road
_vocabulary.village: smaller than a town; fields visible from the last house
_vocabulary.fen_town: built on water — stilts, platforms, boats for streets
_vocabulary.hold: a defended place; drill-yards, walls, people who train
_vocabulary.eyrie: high and wedged; reached by climbing
_vocabulary.skyhold: floating, or so high it may as well be
_vocabulary.underplace: below ground — cavern, tunnel, chamber, stair
_vocabulary.bridge: a crossing, and the town that keeps it
_vocabulary.road: a way between, with places on it
_vocabulary.harbour: where water meets the land and things are landed
_vocabulary.works: where a trade is done — forge, yard, salvage, demolition
_vocabulary.hall: one important room, and the building round it
_vocabulary.temple: a body of practice with a roof
_vocabulary.hermitage: where people go to be alone on purpose
_vocabulary.terrace: a cut level on a slope
_vocabulary.pole: ⛔ a POLE — a pure extremity of an axis, not a settlement. Draw these differently.
_vocabulary.strange: ⚠️ the rules are not steady here
_vocabulary.region: a whole region, not a place you stand in

_siteVocabulary.well: a well or spring people draw water from
_siteVocabulary.green: open common ground inside or beside a settlement
_siteVocabulary.square: the open middle of a place, where people gather
_siteVocabulary.quarter: a part of a town with its own character
_siteVocabulary.mill: a wheel or works driven by water or wind
_siteVocabulary.ford: a shallow place to cross water on foot
_siteVocabulary.yard: an open working ground with a purpose
_siteVocabulary.camp: people staying, under canvas or in billets, not living here

_siteVocabulary.circle: a figure laid on the ground that holds something in
_siteVocabulary.outcrop: bare rock standing out of the land

_siteVocabularyNote: Local-map sites: a site's `kind` is a location kind from _vocabulary or one of these site-scale kinds. Closed: a new value is added here with a one-line meaning before it is used.

mapStates._what: The states every thing on the maps can be in, and the words a player reads for them. The engine keeps one ladder (whole, damaged, ruined, destroyed) and a handful of changes; these are the world's words for each kind of thing. `{name}`, `{old}` and `{from}` are filled in when shown. Build notes stay under `_`. SNG-679.

road.trace: the line of an old road

feature._why: Multiplies what the feature gives (yield, defence, aura, beds, facility). A ruined feature still takes its room; a destroyed one frees it.

hold._why: A hold's own state caps its features: a damaged hold has nothing better than damaged features, a ruined hold nothing better than ruined.

road._why: A blocked road is still walkable, slowly; carts, caravans and moving holds cannot take it. A cut road is gone from the way-finding until it is opened again.

waygate._why: A broken gate is not repaired; it is made again, at the cost of making one.

place._why: A ruin can still be walked to; a razed place is a trace on the map and roads no longer end there.

water._why: Applies to the water-fed features of places and holds on that water: mills, docks, fisheries.

ground._why: Applies to the features worked from that ground: fields, herds, quarries.

buildWorth._why: What a thing with no hold feature is worth to build, in crystal, for repairCost and the player's reward. Scaled against the Water Wheels (40): a stretch of road is less than a mill, a river brought back is more, a place is worth what it houses (its local_ground dwellings), and a gate is the dearest thing on the ground. A Reach pays the same figure in scrip.

repairCost._why: A fraction of the thing's build cost to bring it back to whole. Destroyed is a full rebuild.

repair._ruling: One world. A change made in one game is a change in every game, folded the way shared fates are. A damaged thing stays damaged until someone mends it: the locals, who then go after whoever did it, or a player, who may be rewarded. SNG-679 Part R.
repair._localsWillNot: A razed place has no locals left to rebuild it; a broken gate needs a maker; a dried river is beyond a village. Holds and their features belong to their keepers, not to the locals. These wait for a player.
repair._playerReward: A player who does the work is paid the value of the repair (repairCost x build) in the Reach's scrip or crystal, never coin, and gains standing with the community. Work shared with the locals is paid in proportion. First cut, Erik rules the numbers.

reckoning._what: What the locals do when they bore the repair themselves. A debt for the damages, held by a named local, and someone sent to find whoever did it. Builds on the debt ladder (holdings.js recordDebt / advanceDebts). SNG-679 Part R.
reckoning._search: Days of searching before the one sent finds the culprit, on top of the travel to where the culprit is. A culprit with a hold is looked for there first. Unseen damage is not traced by the locals themselves: they mend it and remember, and post an investigation job (jobs.labels.investigate) that anyone may take.

words.asking: People from {place} are asking after whoever {did} the {thing}.
words.sent: {name} has been sent from {place} to find whoever {did} the {thing}.
words.mending: The people of {place} are at work on the {thing}.

jobs._what: Mending is work on the job list, like any other job: do it yourself, send people, or assign a band. One job brings a thing up one rung (destroyed to ruined, ruined to damaged, damaged to whole). Erik, 2026-10-06: they are like quests you can delegate or assign people to, or just do yourself. SNG-679 R6.
jobs._board: At most three mending jobs on a board at once, nearest first, from things the character knows of within two days of where they are or of one of their holds. The place card lists them all.
jobs.giftLine: Done as a gift. Nothing asked.
jobs._hunt: Erik, 2026-10-06: the hunt for the culprit is a local job. The locals post it to nearby boards; anyone but the culprit may take it. The bounty is a share of the repair value, paid by the locals, so it adds to what the culprit owes. If nobody takes it within localsSendAfterDays, the locals send their own. Unseen damage posts an investigation instead; finding the culprit turns it into a hunt. SNG-679 R7.
jobs._makeGood: Erik, 2026-10-06: the culprit is offered the chance to make good, and may decline it. Offered once, first on their board; declining takes it off and costs nothing by itself. The debt and the hunt go on either way, and the offer comes back in the scene when they are found.

mapStates._numbers: First cut. Erik rules the numbers.

_poleWarning: ⛔ 12 locations are `pole` — pure extremities like the Blaze, the Scouring, the Numen. THEY ARE NOT TOWNS and an icon that says 'settlement' would lie about the most dangerous places in the world. ⚠️ They want their own mark.
_regionDisplay: ⛔ SNG-426 (Erik): 'you have STAIRS as the Harmonic Heights Lower Terrace. That should be HARMONIC HEIGHTS at this region view, period, and a TOWN icon. Once clicked to go local, then you show the lower terrace and upper terrace.' ⚠️ HE IS RIGHT AND THE RULE GENERALISES: A REGION MAP NAMES PLACES; A LOCAL MAP NAMES PARTS OF A PLACE. `regionName` and `regionKind` below override `name` and `kind` AT REGION SCALE ONLY. Where absent, the location's own name and kind stand. ⛔ THE LOCAL TIER IS UNAFFECTED — the terraces are still terraces once you are inside.

harmonic_heights_terrace.why: ⛔ The location IS the lowest terrace, but at 645 miles across the map should say HARMONIC HEIGHTS. The terraces are local-tier features and are already authored there.

radiant_plateau_edge.why: Same rule — 'Edge District' is which part of it you arrive at, not what it is.

old_switchback.why: ⚠️ Keeps `road` — it genuinely is one, and that is the honest icon at any scale.

echo_river_crossing.why: ⛔ `bridge`, not `waygate`. The waygate is the old bridge-stone AT the crossing — a local-tier feature. At region scale this is the town that keeps the only crossing of the Echo.

greywater_stilts.why: 'Stilts' is how it is built, which the icon already says.

thornwake_glade.why: ⚠️ 'Glade' is the local feature; the place is Thornwake.

the-low-lamp-inn.why: ⛔ A SITE OF RADIANT PLATEAU EDGE, sitting at 0.00° from it. Suppressed at region scale — it is a room in a district and appears on the Plateau's local map.

the_hundred_markets.why: Between the Crossing and the Great Coliseum, half a day out: a place you go to, so it keeps its own mark at region scale.

the_quiet_house.why: A little way out from the Crossing, most of a day's walk, because quiet is easier there: a place you go to, so it keeps its own mark at region scale.

the_axis_gate.why: ⛔ Kept — it is the gate OF the Crossing but it is 12 days out, so it is a place you travel to.

_suppressionRule: ⛔ GENERAL RULE, and it fixes the label collisions too: ANY location whose `parentId` is another location AND which sits within 0.5° of that parent is SUPPRESSED at region scale. ⚠️ 24 of the 37 label collisions I measured are exactly this case. An entry in `regionDisplay` is an explicit decision about that place and the general rule does not reach it: `suppressAtRegion` suppresses it, and any other entry (a `regionName`, or only a `why`) KEEPS it. The 0.5° rule decides only the places with no entry.
